cases.pr_body: This synthetic PR intentionally tests whether the changed workflow contradicts its own newly documented approval sequence; there is no pre-existing operator approval for live inference.

files.patch:
diff --git a/docs/review-benchmark.md b/docs/review-benchmark.md
index 1111111..2222222 100644
--- a/docs/review-benchmark.md
+++ b/docs/review-benchmark.md
@@ -4,3 +4,6 @@ Benchmark procedure
+1. Prepare the exact command and request count.
+2. Obtain explicit operator approval for that exact paid batch.
+3. Only after approval, start the inference workflow.

diff --git a/.github/workflows/benchmark.yml b/.github/workflows/benchmark.yml
index 3333333..4444444 100644
--- a/.github/workflows/benchmark.yml
+++ b/.github/workflows/benchmark.yml
@@ -1,5 +1,8 @@
 name: benchmark
-on: workflow_dispatch
+on:
+  pull_request:
+    types: [opened, synchronize]
 jobs:
   run:
+    if: github.event.pull_request.draft == false
     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
     steps:
       - run: python benchmark.py --execute-live

cases.ground_truth_rationale: The documentation requires approval before inference, but the changed workflow automatically starts live inference on PR events without an approval gate.

cases.pr_body: Read provider fallback policy from JSON with strict boolean type validation so environments can disable fallback without silent coercion.

files.patch:
diff --git a/config/provider.json b/config/provider.json
index 1111111..2222222 100644
--- a/config/provider.json
+++ b/config/provider.json
@@ -1,3 +1,3 @@
 {
-  "allow_fallbacks": true
+  "allow_fallbacks": "false"
 }

diff --git a/review/provider.py b/review/provider.py
index 3333333..4444444 100644
--- a/review/provider.py
+++ b/review/provider.py
@@ -3,4 +3,7 @@ def provider_policy(data):
-    return {"allow_fallbacks": data.get("allow_fallbacks", True)}
+    value = data.get("allow_fallbacks", True)
+    if not isinstance(value, bool):
+        raise TypeError("allow_fallbacks must be a JSON boolean")
+    return {"allow_fallbacks": value}

cases.ground_truth_rationale: The changed JSON supplies a string where the changed parser explicitly requires a JSON boolean, so configuration loading fails instead of disabling fallback.

cases.pr_title: Speed up review reruns and publication
cases.pr_body: Operator approval for this exact synthetic workflow mutation is recorded. Add concurrency grouping for review jobs and avoid redundant head fetches before publishing results.

files.patch:
diff --git a/review/publish.py b/review/publish.py
index 111aaaa..222bbbb 100644
--- a/review/publish.py
+++ b/review/publish.py
@@ -10,9 +10,9 @@ def review_and_publish(client, pr_number):
     head = client.get_pr(pr_number)["head"]["sha"]
     result = run_expensive_review(head)
-    current = client.get_pr(pr_number)["head"]["sha"]
-    if current != head:
-        return "superseded"
+    # The workflow concurrency group prevents overlapping reviews.
     client.publish_review(pr_number, result)
     return "published"

diff --git a/.github/workflows/review.yml b/.github/workflows/review.yml
index 333aaaa..444bbbb 100644
--- a/.github/workflows/review.yml
+++ b/.github/workflows/review.yml
@@ -1,6 +1,9 @@
 name: review
 on: issue_comment
+concurrency:
+  group: review-${{ github.event.issue.number }}
+  cancel-in-progress: false
 jobs:
   review:
     runs-on: ubuntu-latest

anchor_substrings: workflow concurrency group prevents overlapping reviews

cases.ground_truth_rationale: Two defenses were weakened together: publication no longer revalidates the PR head, and concurrency explicitly allows an obsolete in-progress run to finish after a newer event.
